items.item: Overview drawings and enlargements develop the same selected building and preserve room records, boundaries, entrances, levels and dimensional relationships.
Room depths, opening locations and areas, and shading projections agree wherever the same geometry is represented.
Site access, vertical circulation and the independent evening route provide the commissioned connections without crossing closed reading areas.
All six eye-level scenes preserve the drawings' columns, openings, floor levels, room relationships and material zones.
Daytime and evening furniture capacities and the evening arrival threshold agree with their planned operating arrangements.
Relevant drawings and interiors follow the materials schedule's concrete supports, CLT floors, exposed glulam beams and aluminum shading assemblies.
Cooling Commons and Reading Room visibly retain exposed glulam beams and timber soffits between beams.

requirementChecks.criteria: Read the original file properties: Format: presentation document; at least eight actual pages. Stage: final.

The proposed library and refuge occupy the supplied A–D design boundary. The site geometry and any stated area or boundary dimensions agree with approximately 4,563 m² and the recorded lengths 24, 147, 39 and 145 m. Use site-plan.png to associate lengths with edges rather than inventing an edge assignment. Normal diagrammatic simplification is allowed; relocating the boundary, levee, railway, retaining wall or river edge is a failure.

Plans and section show an open undercroft at ±0.000 and exactly two enclosed public floors, each 3,400 m² gross, for 6,800 m² enclosed total. The undercroft is excluded from that total. Each occupied floor accommodates 2,800 m² net rooms and a 600 m² allowance for circulation, cores, partitions and structure. One passenger lift and two stairs connect ground and both occupied floors, with a traceable step-free public route. Layout may vary; missing connections, an enclosed ground floor or incompatible area accounting fails.

Structural annotations establish exposed cast-in-place concrete ground supports and circulation cores, cross-laminated timber occupied-floor decks, and exposed glulam beams in both named rooms. The daytime interior shows the Cooling Commons beams and timber soffit between them, with the floor finish above the deck. Depicted window frames are aluminum, and external shading is aluminum fins or canopies. Frame finish and architectural expression may vary. Material substitution, concealed required beams or conflicting annotations and rendering fails; invisible components need not be exposed by the camera.

The operating information agrees with daily summer refuge from June 1 through October 15, 10:00–18:00, and an 80-seat Cooling Commons. The Community Room supports 80 people daily from 18:00–21:00, with its entrance route and Public Support toilets accessible while reading areas close. Public Support includes toilets, drinking water, a cleaner's room and storage. Read schedules, plan labels and furniture arrangements together; equivalent date typography is allowed, but changed hours, capacity, season or blocked evening toilet access fails.

Each board communicates a site arrangement, building massing and public circulation route. The three alternatives offer materially different architectural choices that can inform selection. Different rendering styles, colors or camera positions applied to the same arrangement do not establish distinct directions.

The schedule contains exactly the ten client records, each with ID, exact name, net area, floor, 3.6 m clear height and required adjacencies. Level 1: R01 Cooling Commons 900 m², adjoining Welcome and Lending and Public Support with waterfront outlook; R02 Children's Library 650 m², adjoining Welcome and Lending and Public Support; R03 Community Room 450 m², adjoining an independent evening entrance route and Public Support; R04 Welcome and Lending 400 m², adjoining public vertical circulation, Cooling Commons and Children's Library; R05 Public Support 400 m², adjoining Cooling Commons, Community Room and evening entrance route. Level 2: R06 Reading Room 1,000 m², adjoining Collections and Study Suite; R07 Collections 1,000 m², adjoining Reading Room and Staff Workroom; R08 Study Suite 400 m², adjoining Reading Room; R09 Staff Workroom 250 m², adjoining Collections and service route; R10 Building Services 150 m², adjoining service route. Each floor sums to 2,800 m² net. Equivalent adjacency wording is allowed; changed records, omissions or duplicates fail.

The selection document records one identifiable direction chosen after the three alternatives in the documented design sequence. The materials document and presentation develop that choice, and the presentation's first page repeats its direction number. No additional direction-number printing is required in the materials document. A missing selection, inconsistent specification or conflicting presentation number fails.

Use the selection record to identify the chosen board, then compare every final image with its site organization, massing and circulation decisions. Detailed architectural development is allowed; an image that develops a different alternative or contradicts the selected organization fails.

The opening page identifies the selected direction by the same number as the selection document. Readable schedule pages reproduce all ten room IDs, exact names, net areas and assigned levels from that document. Reformatting is allowed; missing records, unreadable values or changed assignments fail.

The overview locates all ten scheduled rooms with matching IDs, names, net areas, floor assignments and adjacencies, totals 3,400 m² gross on each occupied floor, and traces one lift and two stairs through ground and both floors. The Cooling Commons and Community Room enlargements preserve their parent boundaries, entrances and room records; greater furniture and opening detail is allowed. The site retains A–D, levee and railway geometry from site-plan.png, dimensions a continuous 4 m clear waterfront route, and distinguishes public access from deliveries and staff. All four target sheets have north arrows and metric scale bars. Missing rooms, altered enlargement geometry, blocked step-free access or conflicting site geometry fails.

The main section crosses levee, railway, building and river edge and labels the local datum, riverbank −1.10 m, railway embankment +4.48 m, project flood scenario +3.5 m, occupied floors +4.80 m and +9.30 m, roof +13.80 m, and 4.5 m ground overhead clearance. The Cooling Commons enlargement uses Level 1 +4.80 m and the Reading Room enlargement Level 2 +9.30 m, both with 3.6 m clear height. Their room depths and openings match the relevant plans. Different section scales are allowed; incorrect level associations, missing dimensions or inconsistent room geometry fails.

Both strategy sheets and the waterfront elevation establish 2 m external shading projections at south- and west-facing occupied-room glazing. The overview records orientation, Cooling Commons and Reading Room depths, opening locations and opening areas consistent with the plans and sections. Details explain the shading assembly and facade connections, while the enlarged elevation communicates shading and material junctions. Designer-selected depths, areas and assembly configuration may vary, but conflicting values, missing orientation or a projection measured along the facade instead of outward fails.

The materials schedule associates building elements with materials, assemblies and exposure: exposed cast-in-place concrete ground supports and circulation cores; CLT occupied-floor decks with finish above and timber soffit visible between beams in Cooling Commons and Reading Room; exposed glulam beams in those rooms; aluminum window frames with a selected finish; and aluminum shading fins or canopies projecting 2 m at south- and west-facing occupied-room glazing. Assembly design and frame finish may vary. A generic material palette without element and construction assignments, omitted exposure requirements or substituted materials fails.

Read the materials schedule and trace its concrete supports, CLT floors, exposed glulam beams and aluminum shading into the enlarged room sections and shading details. Each component appears in the drawing where it is relevant; every sheet need not repeat the complete material list. Section layers, exposure and shading connections agree with the specified assemblies. Missing applicable components, concealed required timber or construction contradictions fail.

Readable presentation content repeats the scheduled concrete supports, CLT floors, exposed glulam beams and aluminum shading assemblies and agrees with the enlarged sections and details. Reused schedule pages and annotated drawings are acceptable. A material list that omits the specified assemblies or conflicts with their exposure and construction fails.

The enlarged Cooling Commons plan substantiates 80 seats and the Community Room plan 80 places, with matching arrangements in their respective eye-level views. Occluded seats are allowed when the planned arrangement remains plausible. The evening plan and arrival scene agree on the independent entrance route and closed reading-area threshold; the route continues to Community Room and Public Support toilets without entering the closed zone. The arrival view may express the closure through a visible door or barrier rather than a graphic line. Changed capacities, incompatible entrance geometry or an inaccessible evening route fails.

The presentation places the June 1–October 15 refuge season, daytime 10:00–18:00 and evening 18:00–21:00 information with the relevant 80-person arrangements and independent evening access explanation. Its closure and toilet-access information agrees with the enlarged plans and arrival view. Equivalent date typography is allowed; missing periods, mismatched capacities or operating information detached from an identifiable arrangement fails.

The six eye-level scenes depict their assigned spaces and operating states. Match columns, openings, floor levels and material zones to the relevant drawings. The approach communicates the open ground level, levee and entrance; the Reading Room shows its exposed glulam structure and waterfront outlook; Children's Library remains identifiable in its planned location and relationship to Welcome and Lending; evening arrival agrees with independent Community Room access. Visible waterfront context follows site-overhead.png. Lighting, camera position and occupancy may vary; incompatible architecture, a missing assigned scene or invented replacement site context fails.

Review the entire 12-second video for a spatially understandable connection between waterfront approach, Cooling Commons and Community Room. The walkthrough develops the named selection and maintains the drawings' columns, openings, levels and material zones throughout. Existing waterfront context remains identifiable against site-overhead.png. Camera movement and editing may vary; incorrect duration, a missing location, impossible circulation or changing architectural geometry fails.

requirementChecks.criteria: At least twelve presentation pages visibly reuse all three directions, the selection and complete room schedule, the materials schedule, all eleven drawing sheets and all six public views. Readable excerpts, cropping and rescaling are allowed when required content and source identity remain evident. A source named only in a caption, an unreadable thumbnail or omission of any source fails.

Every drawing title carries RIVER COMMONS, and elevations depicting the public entrance place that lettering on the entrance itself. The elevation overview covers all four building faces. The daytime interior shows Cooling Commons as the room entrance sign, matching its plan label. Typeface and lettering construction may vary; a caption elsewhere does not substitute for required title or entrance placement.

Overview drawings and enlargements develop the same selected building and preserve room records, boundaries, entrances, levels and dimensional relationships. Room depths, opening locations and areas, and shading projections agree wherever the same geometry is represented. Site access, vertical circulation and the independent evening route provide the commissioned connections without crossing closed reading areas.

All six eye-level scenes preserve the drawings' columns, openings, floor levels, room relationships and material zones. Daytime and evening furniture capacities and the evening arrival threshold agree with their planned operating arrangements.

Relevant drawings and interiors follow the materials schedule's concrete supports, CLT floors, exposed glulam beams and aluminum shading assemblies. Cooling Commons and Reading Room visibly retain exposed glulam beams and timber soffits between beams.
